<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is an open-source, cross-platform React Native module (“react-native-video”) that exposes a `<Video>` component.  
   - It provides a JavaScript/TypeScript interface (in `src/`), plus native implementations for Android (`android/`), iOS (`ios/`), Windows (`windows/`) and Web (`src/Video.web.tsx`).  
   - It also includes Expo plugins (`src/expo-plugins/`), documentation (`docs/`), example apps (`examples/`), build scripts (`scripts/`), and CI/CD definitions (`.github/workflows/`).  

2. Main components to include in your system-design diagram  
   a. JavaScript/TypeScript layer  
     • `src/index.ts` and component files (`Video.tsx`, `Video.web.tsx`)  
     • Type definitions (`src/types/`) and native-specs (`src/specs/`)  
     • Expo plugin glue (`src/expo-plugins/`)  
   b. React Native Bridge  
     • Auto-generated/native-module registration that connects JS to platform code  
     • Spec contracts (`NativeVideoManager`, `VideoNativeComponent`)  
   c. Platform-specific native modules  
     • Android: Kotlin/Java code under `android/src/main/java/...` leveraging ExoPlayer, HLS, DASH, RTSP, caching, DRM, ads  
     • iOS: Swift/Obj-C code under `ios/Video/` using AVPlayer, AVContentKeySession, IMA ads, PiP, caching  
     • Windows: C++/C# code under `windows/ReactNativeVideoCPP*/` implementing React Package, View manager  
   d. External native SDKs & services  
     • ExoPlayer (Android), AVFoundation (iOS), Windows Media Foundation  
     • Google IMA SDK for ads  
     • DRM/license servers (via HTTP/URLSession)  
   e. Tooling & CI/CD  
     • Build/test pipelines in `.github/workflows/` for Android, iOS, JS, docs  
     • Linting/format scripts (`scripts/`)  
     • Package publishing (`package.json`, `react-native-video.podspec`, `release-it.json`)  
   f. Documentation site  
     • Next.js project in `docs/`  
     • API reference, guides, asset pipeline, deployed via GitHub Actions  
   g. Example applications  
     • Bare React Native (`examples/bare`)  
     • Expo managed (`examples/expo`)  
     • Plugin sample (`examples/react-native-video-plugin-sample`)  

3. Relationships & data-flow  
   - Arrows from JS API → React Native Bridge → Native modules → Native SDKs → OS media stacks  
   - Examples import the published JS package and call the `<Video>` API (JS)  
   - Docs site reads TypeScript definitions / Markdown to generate API docs  
   - CI/CD pipelines run tests on each platform, build artifacts, and publish docs  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Bridge pattern: decoupling JS API from platform implementations  
   - Plugin architecture: Expo plugins augment native projects at build time  
   - Modular codegen: each platform’s code is isolated under its directory  
   - Single-repo monolith with multiple packages (code + docs + examples)  

5. Diagram-tailoring guidelines for this open-source library  
   - Emphasize the core JS layer as the entry point for consumers  
   - Show “extension points” (expo-plugins, native-module specs)  
   - Illustrate how new platforms could be added by replicating the native-module folder pattern  

6. Diagram construction recommendations  
   - Use distinct shapes/colors:  
     • Blue boxes for JS/TS components (src, examples)  
     • Green boxes for native modules (android, ios, windows)  
     • Orange cylinders for external services/SDKs (DRM server, Ads SDK)  
     • Purple box for Docs site (Next.js)  
     • Gray box for CI/CD (GitHub Actions)  
   - Label each box clearly with its directory or function  
   - Draw uni-directional arrows for data/control flow:  
     JS → Bridge → Native code → OS/SDK  
     CI/CD → Build → Publish → npm / CocoaPods / docs  
   - Group related components in swimlanes (e.g., Client Apps, Library Core, CI/CD, Docs)  
   - Annotate key protocols and technologies on connectors (e.g., HTTP, react-native bridge, Gradle, Xcode build)  

By following these steps, you’ll produce a detailed, platform-aware system diagram that highlights the library’s structure, extension points, and integration flows—perfect for aligning your team and onboard new contributors.  
</explanation>
